subproblem.title: C^1 limit from locally uniform convergence of derivatives on growing balls
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. Let W_k : R^n -> R^l (k in N), V : R^n -> L and reals R_k with R_k -> +infinity. Assume every W_k is C^1 on the open ball B_{R_k}(0), W_k(0) = 0 for every k, V is continuous, and for every real r the Frechet derivatives DW_k converge to V uniformly on the closed ball Bbar_r(0). Then there is W : R^n -> R^l that is C^1 on R^n and satisfies DW(z) = V(z) for every z in R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (W : ℕ → Rn n → Rn ℓ) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (R : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto R atTop atTop → (∀ k, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (W k) (ball (0 : Rn n) (R k))) → (∀ k, W k 0 = 0) → Continuous V → (∀ r : ℝ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k => fderiv ℝ (W k)) V atTop (closedBall (0 : Rn n) r)) → ∃ W' : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 W' ∧ ∀ z, fderiv ℝ W' z = V z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the construction of the limit W in step 7 of the parent proof (W(z) := integral_0^1 V(tz) z dt and Mathlib hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOn), stated for a general sequence.
1. Tail index. For r >= 0 let k(r) in N satisfy R_k > r + 1 for all k >= k(r); it exists since R_k -> infinity. For k >= k(r), the ball B_{r+1}(0) is contained in B_{R_k}(0). Hence W_k is differentiable at every y in B_{r+1}(0) with derivative DW_k(y), and DW_k is continuous on B_{r+1}(0), because W_k is C^1 on an open set containing it.
2. FTC representation. Fix z in R^n, put r := |z|, and let k >= k(r).
 a. For t in the open interval I := (-1/(r+1), 1 + 1/(r+1)) we have |t z| < r + 1. So g(t) := W_k(t z) has derivative g'(t) = DW_k(t z) z on I (chain rule), and t -> DW_k(t z) z is continuous on [0, 1].
 b. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt), W_k(z) - W_k(0) = integral_0^1 DW_k(t z) z dt.
 c. Since W_k(0) = 0, this gives W_k(z) = integral_0^1 DW_k(t z) z dt.
3. Definition of W and pointwise convergence. Define W(z) := integral_0^1 V(t z) z dt; the integrand is continuous in t because V is continuous. Let z and k be as in step 2. For t in [0, 1], t z lies in Bbar_r(0), so
 |W_k(z) - W(z)| = |integral_0^1 (DW_k(t z) - V(t z)) z dt| <= |z| sup over y in Bbar_r(0) of ||DW_k(y) - V(y)||.
 (Use intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const.) The right side tends to 0 as k -> infinity, by the uniform convergence on Bbar_r(0). Hence W_k(z) -> W(z) for every z in R^n.
4. Differentiability on a ball. Fix r > 0 and the open set O := B_r(0). Consider the shifted sequence W'_j := W_{k(r)+j}.
 a. For every j and y in O, W'_j has derivative DW'_j(y) at y, by step 1.
 b. DW'_j -> V uniformly on O, because O is contained in Bbar_r(0) and shifting indices preserves uniform convergence.
 c. W'_j(y) -> W(y) for y in O, by step 3.
 d. By the theorem on uniform limits of derivatives (hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOn, valid on the open set O), W has derivative V(y) at every y in O.
5. Conclusion. Every y in R^n lies in B_{|y|+1}(0), so W is differentiable everywhere and DW(y) = V(y). Since V is continuous, DW is continuous, so W is C^1 on R^n (contDiff_one_iff_fderiv). QED.

subproblem.title: Arzela-Ascoli with diagonal extraction for uniformly Hoelder maps on growing balls
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0 and K >= 0 real, f_k : R^n -> L (k in N) and reals R_k with R_k -> +infinity. Assume f_k(0) = 0 for every k, and ||f_k(z) - f_k(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for every k and all z, z' in the open ball B_{R_k}(0). Then there are a strictly increasing phi : N -> N and V : R^n -> L such that V(0) = 0, V is continuous, ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n, and for every real r, f_{phi(j)} -> V uniformly on the closed ball Bbar_r(0) as j -> infinity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K : ℝ) (f : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (R : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → Tendsto R atTop atTop → (∀ k, f k 0 = 0) → (∀ k, ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (R k), ∀ z' ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) (R k), ‖f k z - f k z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), StrictMono φ ∧ V 0 = 0 ∧ Continuous V ∧ (∀ z z' : Rn n, ‖V z - V z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun j => f (φ j)) V atTop (closedBall (0 : Rn n) r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Arzela-Ascoli and diagonal-subsequence part of step 7 of the parent proof, stated for a general sequence (there f_k = DW_k).
1. Uniform bounds. For m in N put B^m := Bbar_m(0), a compact set because R^n is proper. Since R_k -> infinity, there is k_m in N with R_k > m for all k >= k_m. Let k >= k_m and z, z' in B^m. Then z, z' and 0 lie in B_{R_k}(0), so ||f_k(z) - f_k(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha. Also ||f_k(z)|| = ||f_k(z) - f_k(0)|| <= K |z|^alpha <= K m^alpha, since t -> t^alpha is monotone on [0, infinity) for alpha > 0.
2. Arzela-Ascoli step. Claim: for every m in N and every strictly increasing psi : N -> N there are a strictly increasing chi : N -> N and g : R^n -> L with f_{psi(chi(j))} -> g uniformly on B^m.
 a. Put j0 := k_m. Since psi(i) >= i for all i, psi(j0 + j) >= k_m for every j.
 b. Let h_j be the restriction of f_{psi(j0 + j)} to B^m, a compact space in the subspace topology. By step 1, h_j is continuous (indeed Hoelder) with values in the closed ball of radius K m^alpha in L. That ball is compact because L is finite-dimensional. So h_j is a bounded continuous function.
 c. The family (h_j) is equicontinuous. Given epsilon > 0, choose eta > 0 with K eta^alpha < epsilon. Then |z - z'| < eta implies ||h_j(z) - h_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha <= K eta^alpha < epsilon for all j.
 d. By the Arzela-Ascoli theorem (BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli), the closure of {h_j : j in N} in the space of bounded continuous functions B^m -> L with the sup metric is compact.
 e. A sequence in a compact metric space has a convergent subsequence (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). So there are a strictly increasing chi' and a bounded continuous h with sup over B^m of ||h_{chi'(j)} - h|| -> 0.
 f. Put chi(j) := j0 + chi'(j), which is strictly increasing. Let g := h on B^m and g := 0 elsewhere. Then sup over z in B^m of ||f_{psi(chi(j))}(z) - g(z)|| -> 0, which is uniform convergence on B^m.
3. Diagonal construction. Choose strictly increasing chi_0, chi_1, ... recursively with step 2:
 a. chi_m comes from step 2 applied to m and psi_{m-1}, where psi_{-1} := id and psi_m := psi_{m-1} o chi_m = chi_0 o ... o chi_m.
 b. Thus each psi_m is strictly increasing, and f_{psi_m(j)} converges uniformly on B^m as j -> infinity, to a limit g_m.
 c. Define phi(j) := psi_j(j).
4. phi is strictly increasing. A strictly increasing map chi : N -> N satisfies chi(i) >= i, so chi_{j+1}(j+1) >= j+1 > j. Since psi_j is strictly increasing, phi(j+1) = psi_j(chi_{j+1}(j+1)) > psi_j(j) = phi(j).
5. Tails of phi are subsequences of each psi_m. Fix m.
 a. For j >= m, phi(j) = psi_m(tau_j), with tau_m := m and tau_j := (chi_{m+1} o ... o chi_j)(j) for j > m.
 b. Each tau_j >= j, so tau_j -> infinity.
 c. Uniform convergence on a set is preserved under reindexing by any index sequence tending to infinity. Hence f_{phi(j)} -> g_m uniformly on B^m.
6. The limit function. For z in R^n pick an integer m >= |z|. Then z lies in B^m, and by step 5 the limit lim_j f_{phi(j)}(z) exists and equals g_m(z). Define V(z) to be this limit; it does not depend on m, by uniqueness of limits.
 a. V = g_m on B^m, so f_{phi(j)} -> V uniformly on every B^m.
 b. For real r choose an integer m >= r. Then Bbar_r(0) is contained in B^m (it is empty if r < 0), so f_{phi(j)} -> V uniformly on Bbar_r(0).
7. Properties of V.
 a. V(0) = lim f_{phi(j)}(0) = 0.
 b. Hoelder bound. Let z, z' be in R^n. Since phi(j) -> infinity and R_k -> infinity, for all large j we have R_{phi(j)} > max(|z|, |z'|), so ||f_{phi(j)}(z) - f_{phi(j)}(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha. Letting j -> infinity, by pointwise convergence and continuity of the norm, ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha.
 c. Continuity. Given z and epsilon > 0, choose eta > 0 with K eta^alpha < epsilon. Then |z' - z| < eta implies ||V(z') - V(z)|| <= K |z' - z|^alpha <= K eta^alpha < epsilon, using K >= 0 and alpha > 0. QED.
proof_key_steps: on Bbar_m(0) the tail k >= k_m is uniformly Hoelder and bounded by K m^alpha (f_k(0) = 0)
Arzela-Ascoli on the compact Bbar_m(0) with values in a compact ball of the finite-dimensional L gives a uniformly convergent subsequence of any subsequence
nested subsequences psi_m converge uniformly on Bbar_m(0); the diagonal phi(j) = psi_j(j) is strictly increasing
each tail of phi is a subsequence of psi_m, so f_{phi(j)} converges uniformly on every Bbar_m(0), hence on every Bbar_r(0)
the limit V satisfies V(0) = 0, the global Hoelder bound by passing to the limit, and is continuous

Source: step 8 of the parent proof, stated for general sequences. There ah_k = a_k(x_k + rho_k .), U_k = DW_k, V = DW, and the frozen coefficients A_k are merged into the constant c_k.
1. Fix a C^1_c map zeta and let T := tsupport zeta, which is compact.
 a. Choose r >= 1 with T contained in Bbar_r(0); compact sets are bounded.
 b. Let Z := sup over z in R^n of ||Dzeta(z)||. It is finite because Dzeta is continuous and vanishes outside T (support_fderiv_subset), so its norm attains a maximum on the compact set T.
 c. Let mu_r be the (finite) Lebesgue measure of Bbar_r(0), and N := sup over Bbar_r(0) of ||V||, finite since V is continuous on a compact set.
 d. Let C_A >= 0 satisfy |A[P][Q]| <= C_A ||P|| ||Q|| for all P, Q; it exists because A is a continuous bilinear map (for example its operator norm, ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm₂).
2. Choose k0 with R_k > r for all k >= k0. For such k, Bbar_r(0) and T are contained in B_{R_k}(0).

 b. F_k is continuous on the open ball B_{R_k}(0): compose the joint continuity of (z, P, Q) -> ah_k(z)[P][Q] with z -> (z, U_k(z), Dzeta(z)). E_k is continuous there by continuity of Psi_k and of evaluation L* x L -> R. F is continuous on R^n because A is continuous bilinear and V, Dzeta are continuous.
 c. Let a function be continuous on an open set O and vanish outside a compact set T contained in O. Then it is continuous on all of R^n, since every point outside O has a neighbourhood disjoint from the closed set T. It also has compact support, so it is integrable, and its integral over O equals its integral over R^n (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
 d. Hence, for k >= k0, the hypothesis gives integral of F_k = integral of E_k over R^n. All integrals below may be computed over Bbar_r(0).
4. Error term. For k >= k0 and z in Bbar_r(0): |E_k(z)| <= |d_k| |z|^alpha ||Dzeta(z)|| <= |d_k| r^alpha Z. This uses |z|^alpha <= r^alpha for 0 <= |z| <= r and alpha >= 0; if alpha = 0 both sides are 1. Since E_k vanishes outside Bbar_r(0), |integral of E_k| <= |d_k| r^alpha Z mu_r -> 0.

4. Integrability lemma. Let g : R^n -> R be continuous on Omega with g(x) = 0 for every x outside T. Then g is integrable on Omega and on R^n, and the integrals of g over Omega and over R^n agree. 6. By (ii) and bilinearity, b(x)[DV(x)][Dzeta(x)] = s g1(x) - s g2(x) for every x in Omega. A set integral over Omega depends only on the values on Omega (setIntegral_congr on the measurable set Omega). subproblem.title: Blow-up limit: compactness of normalized blow-up sequences for divergence-form systems
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers. Notation: L := L(R^n, R^l), the continuous linear maps R^n -> R^l with the operator norm; L* := continuous linear forms on L; Bil := continuous bilinear forms on L, viewed as continuous linear maps L -> L*, written b[P][Q]. B_r(0) is the open and Bbar_r(0) the closed ball; D denotes the Frechet derivative (fderiv); 'C^1_c map' means a C^1 map zeta : R^n -> R^l with compact support; integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure. Let alpha > 0, lam, M and K >= 0 be real. Let W_k : R^n -> R^l, ah_k : R^n -> Bil, Psi_k : R^n -> L*, e_k in R^n (k in N) and real sequences R_k, c_k, d_k satisfy: (a) R_k -> +infinity, c_k -> 0, d_k -> 0; (b) for every k, W_k is C^1 on B_{R_k}(0), W_k(0) = 0, DW_k(0) = 0, and ||DW_k(z) - DW_k(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in B_{R_k}(0); (c) for every k, (z, P, Q) -> ah_k(z)[P][Q] is continuous on B_{R_k}(0) x L x L and Psi_k is continuous on B_{R_k}(0); (d) for all k and P, Q in L: lam ||P||^2 <= ah_k(0)[P][P] and |ah_k(0)[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||; (e) for all k, z in B_{R_k}(0) and P, Q in L: |ah_k(z)[P][Q] - ah_k(0)[P][Q]| <= c_k |z|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| and |Psi_k(z)[Q]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||Q||; (f) for every k and every C^1_c map zeta with tsupport zeta contained in B_{R_k}(0), the integral over B_{R_k}(0) of ah_k(z)[DW_k(z)][Dzeta(z)] equals the integral over B_{R_k}(0) of Psi_k(z)[Dzeta(z)]; (g) |e_k| <= 1 for every k, and ||DW_k(e_k)|| = 1 for all sufficiently large k. Then there exist A in Bil and W : R^n -> R^l such that lam ||P||^2 <= A[P][P] and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q|| for all P, Q in L; W is C^1 on R^n; ||DW(z) - DW(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n; the integral over R^n of A[DW(z)][Dzeta(z)] is 0 for every C^1_c map zeta; DW(0) = 0; and ||DW(e0)|| = 1 for some e0 in R^n.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7 and 8 of the parent proof (compactness and limit equation) together with the subsequence extraction of A_k = ah_k(0) and e_k. The proof uses the sibling lemmas holder_diag_subseq, c1_limit and weak_eq_limit.
1. Frozen coefficients. By (d), |ah_k(0)[P][Q]| <= max(M, 0) ||P|| ||Q||. Hence the bilinear operator norm satisfies ||ah_k(0)|| <= max(M, 0) (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound₂). Bil is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is proper. By Bolzano-Weierstrass (tendsto_subseq_of_bounded) there are a strictly increasing phi_A and A in Bil with ah_{phi_A(j)}(0) -> A in operator norm. (Lean: FiniteDimensional, ProperSpace, the norm and subtraction on Bil are only synthesized with `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3` at tactic level.)
2. Unit vectors. The points e_{phi_A(j)} lie in Bbar_1(0). By Bolzano-Weierstrass in R^n there are a strictly increasing phi_e and e0 with e_{phi_A(phi_e(j))} -> e0. Put phi_1 := phi_A o phi_e, which is strictly increasing.
3. Apply holder_diag_subseq to f_j := DW_{phi_1(j)} with radii R_{phi_1(j)}, exponent alpha > 0 and constant K >= 0.
 a. Hypotheses: R_{phi_1(j)} -> infinity because phi_1(j) -> infinity; f_j(0) = 0 and the Hoelder bound on B_{R_{phi_1(j)}}(0) hold by (b).
 b. It gives a strictly increasing phi_2 and V : R^n -> L such that V(0) = 0, V is continuous, and ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z'.
 c. With psi := phi_1 o phi_2 (strictly increasing), DW_{psi(i)} -> V uniformly on Bbar_r(0) for every real r.
4. Apply c1_limit to W_{psi(i)} with radii R_{psi(i)} and V. Its hypotheses hold by (b) and step 3. It yields W : R^n -> R^l, C^1 on R^n, with DW(z) = V(z) for all z. Hence ||DW(z) - DW(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z', and DW(0) = V(0) = 0.
5. Coefficient bound for the limit equation.
 a. Along psi, ah_{psi(i)}(0) -> A, being a subsequence of the sequence of step 1. So eps_i := ||ah_{psi(i)}(0) - A|| -> 0.
 b. For all P, Q: |ah_{psi(i)}(0)[P][Q] - A[P][Q]| <= eps_i ||P|| ||Q||.
 c. For z in B_{R_{psi(i)}}(0), (e) gives |ah_{psi(i)}(z)[P][Q] - A[P][Q]| <= c_{psi(i)} |z|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| + eps_i ||P|| ||Q|| <= c'_i (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q||, where c'_i := |c_{psi(i)}| + eps_i -> 0.
6. Apply weak_eq_limit with A, ah_{psi(i)}, Psi_{psi(i)}, U_i := DW_{psi(i)}, V, radii R_{psi(i)}, constants c'_i and d_{psi(i)}, and the exponent alpha >= 0. Its hypotheses hold:
 a. R_{psi(i)} -> infinity, c'_i -> 0 and d_{psi(i)} -> 0.
 b. V is continuous, and U_i -> V uniformly on every Bbar_r(0) by step 3.
 c. The joint continuity of ah_{psi(i)} and the continuity of Psi_{psi(i)} hold by (c). U_i is continuous on B_{R_{psi(i)}}(0) because W_{psi(i)} is C^1 on that open ball.
 d. The coefficient bound is step 5, the bound on Psi is (e), and the weak equations are (f).
 Hence the integral of A[V][Dzeta] is 0, that is, the integral over R^n of A[DW][Dzeta] is 0, for every C^1_c map zeta.
7. Legendre bounds for A. For fixed P, Q, step 5b gives ah_{psi(i)}(0)[P][Q] -> A[P][Q]. Passing to the limit in (d) gives lam ||P||^2 <= A[P][P] and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||.
8. Unit gradient. e_{psi(i)} -> e0 with e_{psi(i)} in Bbar_1(0). DW_{psi(i)} -> V uniformly on Bbar_1(0) and V is continuous, so DW_{psi(i)}(e_{psi(i)}) -> V(e0) (TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_comp). By (g), and since psi(i) -> infinity, ||DW_{psi(i)}(e_{psi(i)})|| = 1 for all large i. Hence ||DW(e0)|| = ||V(e0)|| = 1.
9. Conclusion. Steps 4, 6, 7 and 8 give A and W with all the required properties. QED.
